XenotypeDef.label: Squirrel
XenotypeDef.description: The Squirrel represents the farming class in rodent society. This population has a high level of distinction due to their orange-red large ears and tail. Almost all squirrels live in the fields outside the rodent kingdom. Unlike the kingdom, which has limited contact with the outside world, squirrel populations have significant opportunities for trade and interaction with local humans. Although they are friendly and have positive personalities, the squirrels' restless nature, fast speech, and peculiar accent often leave people bewildered.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: The Squirrel represents the farming class in rodent society. They are friendly and have positive personalities, but their fast-paced speech and behavior often leave people confused.

XenotypeDef.label: Hamster
XenotypeDef.description: Strictly speaking, the Hamster is not a particularly independent classification. It is widely believed to be a special group that has naturally diverged and then re-integrated into the larger rodent population. The fierce competition for resources after their divergence resulted in heightened combat abilities, physical strength, and healing capabilities that surpass those of ordinary rodents. However, it also led to their extremely combative nature. Reintegrated hamsters in rodent societies often hold positions related to combat. The tail of the hamster has almost degenerated due to evolution. Additionally, their golden fur color is another distinctive feature.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Hamsters possess physical strength and healing capabilities that surpass those of ordinary rodents, but it has also led to their extremely combative nature. The tail of the hamster has almost degenerated due to evolution, and their golden fur color is another distinctive feature.

XenotypeDef.label: Lab Rat
XenotypeDef.description: The Lab Rat, also known as the "Rodent Test Subject," is an ancient species that can be considered a living fossil. It is believed to be the origin of the diverse rodent races today. As the name suggests, this category of rodents was created for research purposes, with its origins dating back thousands of years to certain autonomous mega-cities on Earth before humans left the planet and their biological experiments. Even today, on the fringes of human space exploration, some groups continue to use them for various experiments. Some escaped lab rats are assimilated into local rodent societies, where there is no discrimination against them. Lab Rats despise being referred to as "test subjects." They possess higher psychic abilities than other rodent races. Genetically engineered modifications have endowed them with a calm temperament and better appearance, but these alterations have also made their genetic makeup unstable.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Lab Rats possess higher psychic abilities than other rodent races. Genetically appearance, but these alterations have also made their genetic makeup unstable.

XenotypeDef.label: Beaver
XenotypeDef.description: The beaver originated from the cold regions of a certain planet. Some unscrupulous contracts transported them here where they didn't belong. They are skilled at cutting down plants, and their flat and sturdy tails are also excellent tools during construction operations.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: The beaver comes from the cold zone of a certain planet in the universe and is skilled at cutting down trees and building structures.

XenotypeDef.label: Guinea Pig
XenotypeDef.description: Guinea pigs are a gentle and rare rodent subtype among the Ratkin. They tend to be social and vocal, with round faces and almost no visible tail, and possess a natural affinity for animals with exceptional taming talent, quickly forming bonds with beasts. Many find roles in caretaking and community life, where both animals and colonists trust them easily. Even though they lack a visible tail, Ratkin culture does not see this as a flaw; instead, their soft appearance and kind temperament make friendships with a Guinea Pig highly prized among other Ratkin.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: A gentle and rare rodent subtype with round features, strong affinity for animals, and a kind temperament; other Ratkin take pride in calling a Guinea Pig their friend.
